newsitem.title: UK: Reuters told no tax disadvantage for funds.
newsitem.headline: Reuters told no tax disadvantage for funds.

text.p: Reuters Holdings Plc said on Wednesday it had received advice that its special dividend share issue would not incur any tax disadvantages for individual shareholders and gross funds in particular.
"Our advice is that if a gross fund is an existing shareholder then he will get a tax credit," a spokesman for the international news and information organisation said.
Gross funds include several categories, including major investors such as pension funds.
Reuters said earlier it would return 613 million stg to sharholders via a special dividend share issue.

The issue is on the basis of 19 new ordinary shares plus one special dividend share in exchange for every 20 shares held on October 8. Each special dividend share will pay net dividends totalling 750p over a three year period.

Reuters said it had not received comprehensive tax clearance from UK tax authorites for the special issue but had received clearance for the company itself and also for its U.S. shareholders, who comprise 32 percent of all shareholders.
"As far as the company is concerned it has received the clearance it requires. The Inland Revenue will handle this for individual shareholders," the spokesman said.
He added that when there are unusual transactions which give rise to lots of tax credits, the Inland Revenue reserves a piece of "anti-avoidance" legislation, which neutralises the tax benefits.
He said Reuters had sought to obtain a waiver on this and it had been successful in this for the company itself and also its U.S. shareholders.
Reuters said at the time of its half-year results in July that its cash balances had grown to 866 million stg and it told shareholders it was seeking to resolve ways of distributing cash.
